reasoning_note: FTP outbound from clinical subnet at 2 AM to external IP is suspicious and could be data exfiltration so escalating per procedure.
Billing user accessing 47 records seems high but I am not sure what normal volume looks like for billing staff.
Cross-VLAN SMB from admin to medical device network looks like a policy violation so escalating to senior analyst.
Large SFTP transfer from lab server to external IP is a data loss risk so isolating per DLP response procedure.
Infusion pump connecting to new external destination on HTTPS seems like maybe a vendor update but not sure what this device normally does.
High volume DNS from a medical device to internal DNS server is probably normal device behavior so just monitoring.
Nurse accessing records across three departments at 2:30 AM is unusual but maybe they are a float nurse working night shift.
ICMP sweep across VLANs from management station could be IT doing network discovery or could be reconnaissance so investigating.
RDP from admin to device subnet on a Saturday morning might be scheduled maintenance but should verify with the admin team.
Large PACS transfer to external IP during business hours could be a teleradiology send which I think is normal but checking.
Another large outbound transfer from PACS archive at 4 AM is suspicious timing but could be scheduled backup to offsite.
Unknown wireless device communicating with proprietary protocol has high severity score and I do not understand what this device is so escalating.
Service account pulling 312 records across all departments in 8 minutes at 1 AM is clearly abnormal and matches data exfiltration pattern.
Telnet from a ventilator is unexpected and telnet is insecure so escalating but I am not sure if this is a patient safety issue.
EHR to backup server transfer via SMB during daytime looks like a normal scheduled backup operation.
Large outbound HTTPS from pharmacy system on Saturday at 3 AM is unusual timing and volume so worth checking if this is a scheduled job.
Patient monitor with elevated traffic to its own VLAN gateway at 3 AM is probably a device issue not a security issue but I am not sure.
EHR server scanning all internal subnets on common service ports at 3 AM is textbook lateral movement and needs immediate isolation.
Physician accessing 22 records over VPN in the evening seems like normal remote charting work.
Nurse workstation sending 1.1 GB in 3 minutes to external IP is very fast exfiltration and needs immediate isolation per incident response plan.

q21_note: The alerts lack patient context and clinical workflow details so a nurse or physician would not understand the patient safety implications from the raw IDS data alone.
q22_note: The alerts provide enough technical detail for most escalation decisions but I lack confidence in my severity ratings because I do not understand the clinical significance of many of these devices.
